items.followUp: Explain how an enzyme helps a substrate undergo a chemical reaction.

rubric.why: Shows how the enzyme interacts with its substrate.
rubric.description: The substrate binds to the enzyme’s active site, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing substrate binding to the active site or naming the enzyme-substrate complex.

rubric.why: States how enzyme action makes the reaction easier.
rubric.description: The enzyme provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the enzyme lowers activation energy or provides an alternative pathway.

modelAnswer: The substrate binds to the enzyme’s active site, forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
The enzyme provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy.

items.followUp: Name two careers related to biology and state how each uses biological knowledge.

rubric.why: Identifies a biology-related career and its application.
rubric.description: Medicine: doctors use biology to diagnose and treat diseases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for medicine or a medical role linked to diagnosing or treating disease.

rubric.why: Identifies a biology-related career and its application.
rubric.description: Agriculture uses biological knowledge to improve crops and livestock.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for agriculture linked to improving crops or livestock.

rubric.why: Identifies a biology-related career and its application.
rubric.description: Forestry involves managing or conserving forests and their resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for forestry linked to managing or conserving forests.

rubric.why: Identifies a biology-related career and its application.
rubric.description: Fisheries uses biological knowledge to manage fish and other aquatic resources.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for fisheries linked to managing fish or aquatic resources.

modelAnswer: Medicine: doctors use biology to diagnose and treat diseases.
Agriculture: biological knowledge helps improve crops and livestock.
Forestry: biologists manage and conserve forests and their resources.
Fisheries: biological knowledge helps manage fish and other aquatic resources.

items.followUp: Name the three types of plastids and give one function of each.

rubric.why: Defines plastids and identifies their location and structure.
rubric.description: Plastids are double-membraned organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying plastids as double-membraned organelles in plant cells.

rubric.description: Chloroplasts are a type of plastid.

rubric.why: States the key pigment and function of chloroplasts.
rubric.description: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chlorophyll with photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Identifies chromoplasts and their role in colour.
rubric.description: Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chromoplasts and stating their pigment or colour role.

rubric.why: Identifies leucoplasts and their storage role.
rubric.description: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming leucoplasts and stating that they store food.

modelAnswer: Plastids are double-membraned organelles found in plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.

items.followUp: What is the difference between Rh-positive and Rh-negative blood?

rubric.why: States the basis of the ABO classification.
rubric.description: The ABO system is based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying A and B antigens on red blood cells as the basis of ABO classification.

rubric.description: The four ABO groups are A, B, AB and O.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all four groups.

rubric.why: Describes the antibodies associated with ABO groups.
rubric.description: Plasma contains antibodies against the A or B antigens absent from a person’s red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that plasma antibodies are directed against absent A or B antigens.

rubric.why: States the basis of the Rh classification.
rubric.description: The Rh system depends on whether the Rh antigen is present on red blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the Rh antigen on red blood cells as the basis of the Rh system.

rubric.description: A person with the Rh antigen is Rh-positive; a person without it is Rh-negative.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing Rh-positive and Rh-negative blood by the presence or absence of the antigen.

modelAnswer: The ABO system classifies blood according to the presence or absence of A and B antigens on red blood cells.
The four ABO groups are A, B, AB and O. Group A has A antigen, group B has B antigen, group AB has both, and group O has neither.
The plasma contains antibodies against the A or B antigens that are absent from a person’s red blood cells.
The Rh system depends on the presence or absence of the Rh antigen on red blood cells.
A person with the Rh antigen is Rh-positive; a person without it is Rh-negative.
